To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the MLL third finger is necessary for MML-ENL-induced stem cell immortalization.
loss of the MLL PHD3 domain is necessary for the immortalization of hematopoietic cells by the MLL-EN1 fusion protein.
the loss of the MLL third finger cassette is a critical step in leukemogenesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that lead to the transformation of hematopoietic cells and the development of acute leukemia.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms of MLL-EN1-induced leukemogenesis.
the role of the PHD3 finger of MLL in leukemogenesis and the mechanism by which it regulates the MLL function in hematopoietic cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MLL fusion proteins are able to block differentiation of HSCs by constitutive over-expression of HOX genes and other target genes, leading to immortalization of the HSCs.
MLL fusion proteins are able to immortalize hematopoietic progenitors and that this immortalization is due to their ability to activate the expression of MLL target-genes.
the PHD finger of the MLL protein plays an important role in the repression of MLL target gene, such as the HOX gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the loss of PHD finger 2 and 3 of MLL is a necessary step in the MLL-ENI-induced immortalization of hematopoietic progenitors and that this loss is mediated through the loss of the ability of the MLL fusion proteins to interact with the Cyp33 and HDAC1.
loss of PHD fingers of MLL is necessary for Mll-Enl-induced immortalization of hematopoietic progenitor cells.

the loss of the third PHF of MLL is necessary for Mll-Enl-induced hematopoietitc stem cell immortalization and that the binding of cyclophilin to the MLL 3rd PHF switches MLL from a transcription activator to repressor.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the MLL third finger is essential for the MLL-ENI-induced hematopoietc stem cell immortalization and that it is the binding of CYP33 to the Mll PHD fingers that switches the MLL from transactivation to transcriptional repression.
the PHD finger domains are important in MLL-related leukemia, and that the loss of these domains may be a necessary event in MLL-related oncogenesis.
the PHD fingers play a critical role in the MLL-EN1-mediated immortalization of hematopoietic cells.
